title: Armitage 21 October
when: Online auction closing Wednesday 21 October 2026, each lot at its own time (ADST). The catalogue is going up in parts on Friday 16 October.
deadline: Each lot closes at its own time on Wednesday 21 October; the time is on every card and on the lot page countdown. Bid before the lot's own close.
viewing: Viewing on Wednesday 21 October from 8:30 AM at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay. Phone (03) 6326 2555.
bottom_line: All five catalogues (lots 1 to 600, 601 to 952, 953 to 1286, 1349 to 1677 and 1681 to 1968) are fully checked: every photo was viewed and scoring was blind to the estimate and bids. Lots 1 to 600 (posted Monday 19 October): the find of the sale is Robbery Under Arms, the 1888 Remington three-volume first edition in original cloth (lot 39, estimate $20 to $30): a rebound copy made $6,500 hammer at Australian Book Auctions in May 2024, so keep max $5,300 and flip max $4,095, subject to checking all three volumes at the viewing. Also from lots 1 to 600: a Montblanc Sartorial backpack (18, keep max $410), a carved fruitwood putto (106, $235), a mid-century teak surfboard coffee table (80, $225), a Satsuma tea set (162, $210), Art Deco ceiling lights (239, $200), a Meopta enlarger (552, $170), a Coogan's Tasmania cabinet (528, $155) and pre-war Australian tobacco cards (182, $145). The Singer 222K (142) verifies at $245, below its $305 bid. Two lots with no sold comp but real interest: a Jantzen Sunshine Superman poster (360, dealers ask $1,000 to $1,250) and a pictorial Wallis Island tapa (89). Same-estate books (added 20 Oct): lot 943, Warburton's Journey Across the Western Interior (1875 first edition) with The Fortieth and The Twelfth, keep max $635 from Australian Book Auctions results; lot 924 Victoria Illustrated Second Series (no comp). From lots 601 to 1968: Best supported: a 9ct gold bangle, 34.8 g (lot 886, keep max $1,330, bid $700 when checked), a Louis Vuitton Initiales reversible belt (746, keep max $530, bid $50), 15ct cufflinks (905, $490), an old joiner's workbench (1937, $340), a 16-drawer workshop drawer bank (1828, $295), 9ct rose gold cufflinks (904, $260), a La-Z-Boy power recliner (1227, $245), three small Pro Hart hand-coloured etchings (764, 766, 785, about $170 to $185 each), a French carriage clock (661, $210), a Keith Naughton oil (1108, $210) and a Geoff Tyson watercolour (1013, $210). Seen at the viewing on 17 Oct: the Tudor Oyster (883) is a ref 7934 of about 1957-58 with an original honeycomb dial and Rolex-signed crown, keep max $620 on the lowest sold comp, and worth more to the right buyer. Look at the viewing: a Dior saddle pouch (818), an 18ct Hunt & Roskell pocket watch (874), S. Kirk & Son sterling (642), a complete Endemic Flora of Tasmania (683), an enclosed Shoprider cabin scooter (1159) and packs of new Tasmanian oak lining. From lots 1349 to 1677: an early brass-bladed electric desk fan (1412, $210), a Cyclops pedal car (1355, $190) and several James Bond diecast collections ($70 to $90 each); look at the 1975 Mercedes 280S (1349), a Honda Legend coupe (1354), a Lister D-type engine (1677) and a Hot Toys quarter-scale Batman (1424).

assumptions: Every lot in each catalogue was taken from Armitage's public group page, and every lot page and every photo was fetched at full size. Nothing was bid, watched, logged in to or submitted.
Scoring is blind to price: the Armitage estimate, current bid and bid count were removed from the data the scan, rescore and research agents saw. They are shown on this page for information only.
Buyer's premium is 22% including GST on the hammer price, as shown on every lot page. All-in = hammer x 1.22.

Candidates with a blind score of 4 or more got a market pass (Tasmanian past results first: Armitage's own and Gowans' public results, then other auction houses, marketplaces and dealers). Every flagged lot was then re-checked by Opus, which re-read the photos and opened every comp, dropping any that did not match.

Maximum bids use only sold prices for the same item in similar condition. The first pass used sales from the last 24 months; at the owner's instruction the window was widened to 10 years, which added maximums only where an older sale was the only blocker (lots 32, 64, 363, 1356, 1677, 1742), all marked Low confidence, and never lowered a maximum already set. Melt value for gold and silver is a floor, not a sale, so it never sets a maximum bid.

Flip maximums allow for selling costs (changed 19 Oct at the owner's instruction). Most flip workings already took selling fees and postage off the likely resale price. Where they had not (lots 39, 89, 883 and the six 10-year-window lots), a 15% seller's commission is now taken off. The flip maximum is the higher of: net resale at least double your all-in cost, or net resale at least $500 more than your all-in cost. All-in = hammer x 1.22. Your time is not costed. Keep maximums are unchanged.
Gold and silver weights, carat marks and maker claims in the titles are catalogue claims. Check weights and hallmarks at the viewing.
Pickup only from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay. Inbound freight assumed $0 (local).
Sources closed to this session (eBay, Wine-Searcher, Australian Whisky Auctions) were not used directly.
viewing_notes: Lot 3 (12:31 pm), Malot: open Sans famille tome I to the TITLE page. FIRST EDITION = 'E. Dentu, 1878' with NO edition statement (no 'dixième édition', '31e', '47e' etc.) and NO 'Ouvrage couronné par l'Académie française'. Only if it passes: one 1878 first sold for EUR 5,040 incl. premium at Christie's Paris on 5 Jul 2023 (contemporary half chagrin), about A$8,100, so keep max up to about $6,600. It is probably a later printing (it is bound to match an 1895-or-later En famille); if so, dealers ask EUR 30 to 200 a set and it is not worth chasing.

Lot 25 (12:38 pm): CONFIRMED by the owner, The Little Black Princess is the 1905 first edition. NEW keep max $380, flip $160 for the whole lot, from sold prices: 1905 first $280 (Leski, Mar 2022) plus the six Bean volumes at about $31 a volume. Check the printing dates in the six Bean volumes (first printings add value) and whether Modern Crusaders is the 1919 first and unsigned.

Lot 39 (12:42 pm): Robbery Under Arms, worn original cloth. NEW keep max $1,800 (lowest same-edition sale A$2,200, SRBA 2019; a fine original-cloth copy made US$2,400 incl. premium at Sotheby's NY 2024; the A$6,500 ABA copy was the outlier). Check vol I for its half-title and title leaf (look for stubs); if missing, stop near $1,000. ABA lot 97 on Invaluable has only one photo, of the calf spines.

Lot 943 (5:43 pm): Warburton 1875 + The Fortieth + The Story of the Twelfth. Keep max $760. Unfold the Warburton's large folding map: complete copies in original cloth with the map made A$500 to 1,300 (ABA) and GBP 625 to 1,625 (Sotheby's London); a rebound copy made A$240 and a copy with no map only A$80. Without the map, stop near $450; check the frontispiece, 8 plates and half-title.

Lot 924 (5:37 pm), Victoria Illustrated Second Series 1862, and lot 7 (12:40 pm), an S.T. Gill plate from the first series: likely the same estate. No sold comp for the 1862 second series (the 1857 first series makes $600 to $2,200 at ABA), so no maximum. Count the plates in 924 and check the binding. No bids on 924 yet.

Lot 31 (12:40 pm), 13 uniform Stevenson volumes in tan buckram: open one and look for an edition name and a limitation statement on the half-title or title verso (for example a numbered collected edition). If it is a plain reprint, ignore it.
Lot 883 (5:24 pm): Tudor Oyster 7934. Wind it and watch the seconds hand; check the crown screws down.

Lot 89 (about 1 pm), Wallis tapa: turn it over. Hand-beaten bark cloth is fibrous and slightly felted with overlapping joins; machine-flat or canvas-like means a reproduction. Natural paint sits in the fibres; bright, even, plasticky paint on top means modern acrylic. Look for insect holes, tears, brittleness, stains, and any old collection label or inked number on the back or sleeves. If it is old and sound, keep max $725. If it looks recent, bid $100 to $150 at most. Webb's Material Culture (Auckland) appraises for free from photos. Extra context: a 232 cm 'Wallis Island' tapa reportedly sold at Woolley & Wallis (UK) in Sept 2023 for GBP 1,310 (about A$2,500); its imagery is not confirmed pictorial and I could not open the price, so it sets no maximum. SEEN 19 Oct (owner's photos): the back is felted, fibrous hand-beaten bark cloth with an overlap seam, and the paint is soaked into the fibres, so it is genuine tapa. The listing photos show the pictorial type (village scene plus canoe, lobster, crab, octopus, fish, ray, with 'Mua Wallis' lettered on the sail), the same type as Te Papa FE012568. The back is pale and even, so probably mid-to-late 20th century. Still to check: whether the glossy red-brown borders are a later coating, and the small white specks on the red (dust or mould).
Lot 18 (12:35 pm), Montblanc backpack: serial or authenticity tag, base and corners, strap edges, zips.
Lot 746 (4:38 pm), Louis Vuitton belt: date code or heat stamp, size stamp, back of the buckle, reverse side. Do not bid if authenticity is doubtful.
Lot 905 (5:31 pm), 15ct cufflinks: read the 15ct mark; stones firm; chains and bars intact. Lots 904 and 885: the carat marks.
Lot 661 (4:10 pm), carriage clock: ask to wind it; check it runs, strikes and repeats.

Lots 239, 106, 162, 80, 182, 122 (1 to 1:30 pm): 239 shade rims and wiring (needs rewiring); 106 hairline cracks and the ring; 162 bases for marks; 80 veneer lifting and wobble; 182 whether the card sets are complete; 122 whether the drawers run.
Lots 766, 680, 1108, 1013 (pictures): signatures, edition numbers, foxing under glass, and the back of the Naughton oil.

Lots 1227, 1100, 1937, 1828, 1412, 1677, 1070, 1075, 1476 (evening): recliner motors; rug back for repairs and moth; workbenches for woodworm and splits (1828 has later replacement drawers); fan cord and wiring; Lister engine turns over, compression, magneto spark; pedal organ reeds; lustres for chips; DS lower screen is hazy.
Lots 874, 872, 818, 750, 683, 642, 365, 1424, 7, 29, 360, 1349, 1354 have no maximum bid. If one checks out, tell me and I will look for a sold comp.
Do not chase lots 142 (Singer) or 886 (gold bangle): both are bid past the keep maximum.
BOOK RE-CHECK (20 Oct): 58 book and paper lots re-read photo by photo for first editions and other valuable printings. Nothing else is clearly valuable from the photos. Checks to make in person:

Lot 7 (12:32 pm), Gill plate: a framed Gill frontispiece with another framed print sold for A$20 at Leski in May 2026, and this exact pair passed twice at Lawsons (top bid A$50). Stay under about $20 to 50. Check for a real plate mark (about 17.6 x 25.5 cm) and raised ink lines; the 1890s facsimiles are photolithos. Photograph the loose coloured vignette front and back (still unidentified).
BOOK RE-CHECK lot 172 (1:28 pm): open the Gothic-panelled leather volume; it may be a carte-de-visite album with Tasmanian studio photos. The three Heyers are later reprints.
BOOK RE-CHECK lot 223: read the title pages of the four small books (two leather-backed) for an early Hobart, Launceston or Sydney imprint.
BOOK RE-CHECK lot 237: the 6 July 1929 Keith Anderson (Kookaburra) memorial order of service. Check it is complete and whether the newspapers are originals and their dates. No comps.
BOOK RE-CHECK lot 238: open all nine Penzig Sandy Creek Bushranger copies for a signature or number.
BOOK RE-CHECK lot 286: test the Don McLean signature on the poster (marker ink sits on the surface; a print is flat with a dot pattern).

BOOK RE-CHECK lot 296 (2:08 pm): look inside Perucho's Joan Miro y Cataluna for a loose colour lithograph signed in pencil and numbered (x/100). If it is there: the complete book with the lithograph sold for GBP 3,024 at Sotheby's in Sep 2022 (about A$5,770), so up to about $4,700; the lithograph alone has made US$950 to 1,100 hammer (about A$1,360 to 1,575). Without it, ignore the lot.

BOOK RE-CHECK lot 561 (3:37 pm): Klee, The Thinking Eye. A 1961 first English edition sold for US$130 hammer in 2017 (about A$185). Worth up to about $150 for the lot only if the back of the title page says 'First published 1961' with no reprint line. Otherwise a $30 bulk lot.
BOOK RE-CHECK lot 799: Mortmain no. 310 of 500; Gowans sold a copy for $60 in Sept 2026, so keep max about $49.

BOOK RE-CHECK lot 819: find the 'signature' the catalogue mentions (none shows in the photos). Lot 840: the Fleming is a first impression, trade issue; check for a jacket (worth much more with one). Lot 924: count the plates (engraved title plus 43). Lot 993: the Gould is a facsimile. Lots 941, 942, 996: signed limited Lansdowne folios; check foxing and slipcases.
Lot 993 (6:00 pm area), Gould Birds of Australia FACSIMILE (Lansdowne 1979): sold alone A$180 (Theodore Bruce 2019) and A$240 (Lawsons 2021), so keep max $145.
